sentences.text: Palaealectoris belongs to the Tetraonidae family.
Its upper arm bone displayed a crest similar to that seen in chachalacas, suggesting a convergent adaptation.
A broken leg bone was collected in May 1925 near Chesapeake Beach, Maryland, by Remington Kellogg and Norman Boss.
The holotype, the specimen the species is based on, was gathered in the summer of 1928 by Erich Maren Schlaikjer in Nebraska.
Alexander Wetmore formally named the genus in 1930 using a fragment of a left humerus.
Remains from Nebraska and Maryland date to the Early Miocene, specifically between 23.1 and 18.5 million years ago during the Chattian to Burdigalian stages.
